scenes.name: Pub rock y primeros indies
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Justo antes del punk nacen Chiswick (Count Bishops, 1975) y Stiff (Nick Lowe, 1976), sellos independientes surgidos del pub rock pero dirigidos por veteranos de la industria que enseguida se asocian con las distribuidoras grandes: Stiff se convierte en la máquina de hits new wave de Ian Dury y Elvis Costello.
scenes.family: Antecedentes: punk, art rock, kraut y glam

podcast.title: Disbandment After Sex Pistols Show (April 3, 1976)
podcast.body: Joe Strummer realized The 101ers were "going nowhere" after attending a Sex Pistols concert at The Nashville Rooms in Kensington, London, on April 3, 1976. He recognized that the Sex Pistols' raw energy represented "the future," prompting him to seek a new musical direction which led to the formation of The Clash.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation and Name Origin
podcast.body: Sometime in 1974, after busking in London, Joe Strummer (then John Miller) rounded up friends to form a group called The 101ers. The band's name comes from "the number of the house in West London where all the band members lived."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: London Flat
podcast.body: The members of The 101ers resided together in a flat located at 101 Walter Tinteres in London. "Bunch of guys lived in a flat and 101, Walter Tinteres in London. They played in a group which they called appropriately enough the 101ers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Very First Episode of the Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Nashville Club Gig (Pre-Clash)
podcast.body: The band had a gig at a club called Nashville where the Sex Pistols performed as the opening act. This event proved pivotal as their guitar player, Joe, was so impressed by the Sex Pistols' attitude and energy that he subsequently left The 101ers to form The Clash. "One night they had a gig at a club called Nashville."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Very First Episode of the Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pub Circuit Success and Horn Section
podcast.body: The 101ers achieved considerable success on the London pub circuit, playing covers of American R&B songs. At one point, the band even featured a full horn section composed of "guys in the run from the evil regime in Chile," adding a unique element to their sound.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation History
xref.body: Joe, the guitarist for The 101ers, was profoundly influenced by the Sex Pistols' attitude and energy when they opened for his band at the Nashville club, despite their "awful" musicianship. A few days later, Joe left The 101ers and began forming a new band with others who admired the Sex Pistols. This new group went through several name changes—The Psychotic Negatives, The Weak Heart Drops, The Outsiders, The Mirrors in the Evening Standards—before finally settling on The Clash. "It was their attitude and their energy that grabbed his attention."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Very First Episode of the Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Joe Strummer's Background
xref.body: The last member to join the group was Joe Strummer, whose real name was John Millers. He was a "refugee" from a pub rock band called The 101ers and insisted on being addressed by his new moniker. Millers, the son of an international diplomat, had a somewhat "posh" upbringing but intentionally abandoned it to become a busker. He earned the name "Strummer" due to the intense ferocity with which he played his guitar. "The last member of the group to join was a refugee from a pub rock band called the 101ers, and he insisted on being addressed as Joe Strummer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Joe Strummer's Background and Joining
xref.body: The singer, Joe Strummer, was a busker with a "secretly posh background" as the son of a diplomat. He was the last member to join, convinced to defect from a pub rock band called The 101ers. "He called himself Joe Strummer, and he was the last to join when he was convinced to defect from a pub rock band called the 101ers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Opening Act for The 101ers – Nashville Club
xref.body: The band opened for The 101ers at a club called Nashville. Despite their "awful" musicianship, their attitude and energy profoundly impressed Joe, the guitarist for The 101ers, motivating him to leave his band and form The Clash. "It was their attitude and their energy that grabbed his attention."
